plain_english: Now the fourth chapter: the Lord said, thus I taught the imperishable yoga to Vivasvat; Vivasvat spoke it to Manu, and Manu declared it to Ikshvaku.
sanskrit_cite: atha caturtho'dhyāyaḥ   śrībhagavānuvāca   evaṃ vivasvate yogaṃ proktavānahamavyayam | vivasvānmanave prāha  manurikṣvākave'bravīt

plain_english: Thus royal sages knew this tradition-received yoga, but it was lost in great time, scorcher of foes; and though obtained by teacher lineage, it is now lost; by this the Lord shows the rarity and weight of this knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ paramparāprāptamimaṃ rājarṣayo viduḥ | sa kāleneha mahatā  yogo naṣṭaḥ parantapa | etacca guruparamparayā prāptamapi adyatve naṣṭam ityanena  bhagavānasya jñānasya durlabhatāṃ gauravaṃ ca pradarśayati

plain_english: That same ancient yoga has been taught to you today; you are my devotee and friend, and this highest secret is so; by the word ca a secondary sense is said, so devotion here is primary toward the teacher, not friendship; this is the purport. Arjuna, though knowing the Lord's own form, asks in the world to make it clear.
sanskrit_cite: sa evāyaṃ mayā te'dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ | bhakto'si me  sakhā ceti rahasyaṃ hyetaduttamam | bhakto'si me sakhā ceti tvaṃ bhakto matparamaḥ sakhā ca | caśabdenānvācaya ucyate | tena yathā bhikṣāṭane bhikṣāṇāṃ  prādhānyaṃ gavānayane tvaprādhānyam | evaṃ bhaktiratra guruṃ  pradhānaṃ na sakhitvamapīti tātparyārthaḥ | arjuno bhagavatsvarūpaṃ jānannapi loke sphuṭīkartuṃ pṛcchati-

plain_english: Arjuna said: your later birth and Vivasvat's earlier birth—how should I know this, that you taught at first?
sanskrit_cite: arjuna uvāca   aparaṃ bhavato janma paraṃ janma vivasvataḥ | kathametadvijānīyāṃ  tvamādau proktavāniti

plain_english: The Lord said: many births of mine have passed, and yours too, Arjuna; I know all those, but you do not, scorcher of foes.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna | tānyahaṃ veda  sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha parantapa

plain_english: Though unborn and imperishable in self, though lord of beings, presiding over my own nature, I am born by my own maya.
sanskrit_cite: ajo'pi sannavyayātmā bhūtānāmīśvaro'pi san | prakṛtiṃ  svāmadhiṣṭhāya sambhavāmyātmamāyayā

plain_english: When duty declines and unrighteousness rises, the Lord creates a self-portion and takes a body to sustain the world.
sanskrit_cite: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata | abhyutthānamadharmasya tadātmāṃśaṃ sṛjāmyaham | śrībhagavānkila  pūrṇaṣāḍguṇyatvāccharīrasaṃparkamātrarahito'pi  sthitikāritvātkāruṇikatayā ātmāṃśaṃ sṛjati | ātmā-pūrṇaṣāḍguṇyaḥ aṃśaḥ-upakārakatvenāpradhānabhūto  yatra tadātmāṃśaṃ-śarīraṃ gṛhṇātītyarthaḥ

plain_english: For protecting the good, destroying wrongdoers, and establishing duty, I manifest in every age.
sanskrit_cite: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām | dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge

plain_english: Whoever truly knows my divine birth and action leaves the body without rebirth and comes to me.
sanskrit_cite: janma karma ca me divyamevaṃ yo vetti tattvataḥ | tyaktvā dehaṃ  punarjanma naiti māmeti so'rjuna | ata evāsya janma divyaṃ yata ātmamāyayā yogaprajñayā  svasvātantryaśaktyā ārabdhaṃ na karmabhiḥ | karmāpi  divyaṃ-phaladānāsamarthatvāt | yaścaivametattatvaṃ  vetti-ātmanyapyevameva manyate so'vaśyaṃ bhagavadvāsudevatattvaṃ  jānāti

plain_english: Many, purified by knowledge and austerity and absorbed in me, attain my state while doing action without fruit.
sanskrit_cite: vītarāgabhayakrodhā manmayā madvyapāśrayāḥ | bahavo  jñānatapasā pūtā madbhāvamāgatāḥ | tathā caiva vidantaḥ manmayatvātparipūrṇecchatvāt krodhādirahitā  niṣphalaṃ karma karaṇīyaṃ kurvāṇā bahavo matsvarūpamavāptāḥ | yataḥ-

plain_english: As people surrender to me, so I worship them; all follow my path, and I take the form sought by devotees.
sanskrit_cite: ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃstathaiva bhajāmyaham | mama  vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ | p. 111)   ye yayaiva buddhyā māmāśrayante tānprati tadeva svarūpaṃ  gṛhṇaṃstānanugṛhṇāmi | evameva madīyaṃ mārgaṃ manmayā  amanmayāśca sarve evānuvartante nahi jyotiṣṭomādiranyo mārgaḥ  madīyaiva sā tathecchā | vakṣyate hi cāturvarṇya mayā sṛṣṭam  iti | anyastvāha-liṅarthe laṭ | yathā atirātre ṣoḍaśinaṃ  gṛhṇanti-gṛhṇīyurityarthaḥ | evamihāpi  anuvartante-anuvarteranniti

plain_english: Those desiring success in action worship deities here; success born of action occurs quickly in the human world.
sanskrit_cite: kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhiṃ yajanta iha devatāḥ | kṣipraṃ hi  mānuṣe loke siddhirbhavati karmajā | mānuṣa eva loke bhogāpavargalakṣaṇā siddhirnānyatra iti

plain_english: The fourfold order was created by me according to guna and karma; know me as maker yet non-doer and imperishable.
sanskrit_cite: cāturvarṇyaṃ mayā sṛṣṭaṃ guṇakarmavibhāgaśaḥ | tasya  kartāramapi māṃ viddhyakartāramavyayam

plain_english: Actions do not stain me, nor is desire in fruits; one who knows this is not bound by actions.
sanskrit_cite: na māṃ karmāṇi limpanti na me kāmaḥ phaleṣvapi | iti māṃ  yo'bhijānāti karmabhirna sa badhyate | mama kila kathamākāśakalpasya karmabhirlepaḥ | ākāśapratimatvaṃ  kāmanābhāvāt | ityanena jñānaprakāreṇa yo  bhagavantamevāśrayate sarvatra sarvadā ānandaghanaṃ  parameśvarameva na vāsudevātparamasti kiṃcit iti nītyā vimṛśati  tasya kiṃ karmabhirbandhaḥ

plain_english: Knowing this, do action as ancients did; purified by this intelligence, perform necessary actions.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ jñātvā kṛtaṃ karma pūrvairapi mumukṣubhiḥ | kuru karmaiva  tasmāttvaṃ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam | tasmādanayā buddhyā pavitrīkṛtastvamapi  karmāṇi-avaśyakartavyāni kuru

plain_english: Success is not from non-action alone; even poets are deluded here, so I will declare action by knowing which you are freed.
sanskrit_cite: athocyate akaraṇādeva siddhiḥ - iti | tanna yataḥ   kiṃ karma kimakarmeti kavayo'pyatra mohitāḥ | tatte karma  pravakṣyāmi yajjñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt

plain_english: Action, forbidden action, and non-action must be known; the course of action is deep and hard to discern.
sanskrit_cite: karmaṇo hyapi boddhavyaṃ boddhavyaṃ ca vikarmaṇaḥ | akarmaṇaśca  boddhavyaṃ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ | karmākarmaṇorvibhāgo duṣparijñānaḥ | tathā ca-vihitakarmaṇyapi  madhye duṣṭaṃ karmāsti-agniṣṭoma iva paśuvadhaḥ | viruddhe'pi  ca karmaṇi śubhamasti karma | tathāhi hiṃsraprāṇivadhe  prajopatāpābhāvaḥ | akaraṇe'pi ca śubhāśubhaṃ  karmāsti-vāṅmanasakṛtānāṃ karmaṇāmavaśyaṃbhāvāt teṣāṃ  jñānamantareṇa duṣpariharatvāt | ataḥ kuśalairapi  gahanatvātkarma na jñāyate anena śubhakarmaṇā śubhamasmākaṃ  bhaviṣyati anena ca karmaṇāmanārambheṇa mokṣo na bhaviṣyati-iti | tasmādvakṣyamāṇo vijñānavahnirevāvaśyaṃ  sakalaśubhāśubhakarmendhanaploṣasamarthaḥ śaraṇatvenānveṣya-iti  bhagavato'bhiprāyaḥ | tamevodbodhayitumāha-

plain_english: One who sees non-action in action and action in non-action is wise among humans.
sanskrit_cite: karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśyatyakarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ | sa buddhimān  manuṣyeṣu sa coktaḥ kṛtsnakarmakṛt | karmaṇīti-ātmīyeṣu karmasu yaḥ akartṛtvādakarmatvaṃ paśyati  praśāntatayā | akarmasu ca-parakṛteṣu ātmakṛtatvaṃ jānāti  paripūrṇoditasvarūpatvena | sa eva sarvasva madhye buddhimān  kārtsnyena-sākalyenāsau karma karoti | ato'sya kena karmaṇā  phalaṃ dīyatām ityuditadaśāyām | praśāntatve tu kṛtsnāni  karmāṇi kṛntati cchinatti | ataḥ sarvameva karoti na kiṃcidvā  karoti-ityupaniṣat

plain_english: Whose every undertaking is free from desire-intention, and whose actions are burned by the fire of knowledge, him the wise call learned. Hence, abandoning intention regarding desired objects and fruits, actions that are performed enter the fire of knowledge, whose nature is described and to be described, and are burned.
sanskrit_cite: yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāmasaṅkalpavarjitāḥ | jñānāgnidagdhakarmāṇaṃ tamāhuḥ paṇḍitaṃ budhāḥ | ata eva kāmeṣu-kāmyamāneṣu phaleṣu saṅkalpaṃ vihāya  kriyamāṇāni karmāṇi kathitakathayiṣyamāṇasvarūpe  jñānāgnāvanupraviśya dahyante

plain_english: Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of action, ever content and without support, though engaged in action he does nothing at all; though eager and active, he does nothing.
sanskrit_cite: tyaktvā karmaphalāsaṅgaṃ nityatṛpto nirāśrayaḥ | karmaṇyabhipravṛtto'pi naiva kiñcitkaroti saḥ | abhipravṛtto'pi-ābhimukhyena pravṛtto'pi

plain_english: A desireless person with controlled mind and self, having abandoned all possessions, does only bodily action; bodily action is that which is useful to the body and of the nature of sense activity, and it is not tinged by mind and intellect.
sanskrit_cite: nirāśīryatacittātmā tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ | śārīraṃ kevalaṃ  karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam | śarīropayogi indriyavyāpārātmakaṃ karma śārīraṃ  yanmanobuddhibhyāṃ na tathānurañjitam

plain_english: One who is content with what comes by chance, beyond opposites, free from envy, and equal in success and failure is not bound even while acting. Action binds the agent only by taking on the impurity of desire for fruit; the self binds itself. Otherwise, if inert actions themselves bound, freedom in bondage would not be heartfelt.
sanskrit_cite: yadṛcchālābhasantuṣṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ | samaḥ  siddhāvasiddhau ca kṛtvā'pi na nibadhyate | karmakartari prayogaḥ svayameva hyātmā ātmānaṃ badhnāti  phalavāsanākāluṣyamupādadāna ityarthaḥ | anyathā jaḍānāṃ  karmaṇāṃ bandhane svātantryaṃ na tathā hṛdayaṃgamam

plain_english: For one freed of attachment, liberated, mind resting in knowing, acting for sacrifice — all action melts away; and 'for sacrifice' is uttered in the singular, the sacrifices being those described hereafter.
sanskrit_cite: gatasaṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthitacetasaḥ | yajñāyārabhataḥ  karma samagraṃ pravilīyate | yajñāyeti-jātāvekavacanam | yajñāḥ-vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇāḥ

plain_english: The verse says sacrifice in its general nature is brahma offered into brahma-fire by brahma; through brahma-action concentration one goes to brahma. For one engaged, offering in brahma leads to re-entry there. The whole world-souled brahma is the oblation offered in supreme knowledge, in quiet fire, for the increase of radiance. For the yogi whose concentration is such brahma-action, brahma alone is to be gone to and known, and no other fruit is obtained. Limited sacrificers receive limited fruit, while knowers of unlimited complete self-sacrifice do not. The verse binds a supreme secret, explained according to intellect and teacher-tradition; some say instruments and action are brahma-qualifications, but that is to be neglected because the secret tradition-sequence remains unbroken.
sanskrit_cite: yajñāyetyuktam-tatsvarūpaṃ sāmānyaṃ tāvadāha   brahmārpaṇaṃ brahmahavirbrahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam | brahmaiva tena  gantavyaṃ brahmakarmasamādhinā | brahmaṇyarpaṇaṃ-tata eva pravṛttasya punastatraivānupraveśanaṃ  yasya tat | brahma-samagraṃ viśvātmakaṃ yadetat havistat | brahmaṇi-paramabodhe praśānte'gnau | brahmaṇā-yenakenacitkarmaṇā  hutaṃ-taddīptyabhivṛddhaye samarpitam itīdṛśaṃ brahmakarmaiva  samādhiryasya yoginastena brahmaiva gantavyaṃ jñeyaṃ  nānyatkiṃcidanyābhāvāt | yadivā tadarthena  yadarthākṣepādevaṃsaṃbandhaḥ-yatkhalu brahmasvarūpeṇa  yajamānena brahmāgnau brahmahavirhutaṃ brahmaṇi  brahmasvabhāvadevatoddeśenārpaṇaṃ yasya tadevaṃ bhūtaṃ  yadbrahmakarma tadeva samādhirātmasvarūpalābhopāyatvāt  tena-brahmakarmasamādhinā nānyatphalamavāpyate apitu brahmaiveti ye  yathā māṃ prapadyante-iti hi nirvāhitam | mitasvarūpī-kṛtamadātmakayajñasvabhāvā iti  tādṛśaphalabhāginaḥ-ityuktam | aparimitaparipūrṇamadātmakayajñasvarūpavedinastu kathaṃ  parimitaphalalavalāmpaṭyabhāgino bhaveyuriti tātparyam | ityanena | ślokena vakṣyamāṇaiśca ślokeḥ paramarahasyamupanibaddham | taccāsmābhirmitabuddhibhirapi yathābuddhi yathāgurvāmnāyaṃ ca  vivṛtam | mukhasaṃpradāyakramamantareṇa naitat nabhaścitramiva  cittamupārohatīti na vayamupālambhanīyāḥ | atra haviṣo'gneḥ  karaṇānāṃ ca srugādīnāṃ kriyāyāśca brahmaviśeṣaṇatvamiti  kaiściduktaṃ tadupekṣyameva-teṣāṃ  rahasyasaṃpradāyakrame'kṣuṇatvāt

plain_english: Some yogis worship divine sacrifice, others offer sacrifice into brahma-fire, and others offer senses and objects; all obtain self-gain.
sanskrit_cite: daivamevāpare yajñaṃ yoginaḥ paryupāsate | brahmāgnāvapare  yajñaṃ yajñenaivopajuhvati | apare devāni-krīḍāśīlāni indriyāṇi āśritya yaḥ sthito  yajño-nijanijaviṣayagṛhaṇalakṣaṇaḥ tameva parita  upāsate-āmūlādvimṛśanta svātmalābhaṃ labhante | ata eva te  yoginaḥ-sarvāvasthāsu satatameva yogayuktatvāt | nityayoge  hyayamatra matvarthīyaḥ | enameva ca viṣayagṛhaṇātmakaṃ yajñaṃ  yajñenaiva-tenaiva lakṣaṇena apare-pūrayitumaśakye brahmāgnau  juhvati-iti kaiścidyākhyātam | munestu  paurvāparyāviruddhatvādyo'rtho hṛdi sthitastaṃ  prakāśayāmaḥ-kecidyogayuktā santo  daivaṃ-nānārūpendrādidevatoddeśenaiva bāhyadravyamayaṃ  yajñamupācaranti | taṃ ca kriyamāṇameva yajñaṃ  kartavyamidamityeva buddhā phalānapekṣayā apare-duṣpūre  brahmāgnāvarpayanti-iti dravyayajñā api paraṃ brahma yānti | yato  vakṣyate sarve'pyete yajñavidaḥ-iti | śrutirapi yajñena  yajñamayajanta devāḥ-iti

plain_english: Some offer senses into restraint-fires, others offer objects into sense-fires; mind is the fire, and enjoyment is the identity of enjoyer and enjoyed.
sanskrit_cite: śrotrādīnīndriyāṇyanye saṃyamāgniṣu juhvati | śabdādīnviṣayānanya indriyāgniṣu juhvati | anye tu saṃyamāgniṣvindriyāṇīti | saṃyamaḥ-manaḥ tasya  ye'gnayaḥ-pratipannabhāvabhāvanārūpā abhilāṣaploṣakā  visphuliṅgāḥ teṣu indriyāṇyarpayanti | ata eva te tapoyajñāḥ | itare jñānapradīpiteṣu phaladāhakeṣvindriyāgniṣu  viṣayānarpayanti-bhogavāsanānirāsāyaiva  bhogānabhilaṣantītyupaniṣat | tathā ca mayaiva laghvyāṃ  prakriyāyāmuktam   na bhogyaṃ vyatiriktaṃ hi bhoktustvatto vibhāvyate | eṣa eva hi  bhogo yattādātmyaṃ bhoktṛbhogyayoḥ | iti spande'pi   bhoktaiva bhogyabhāvena sadā sarvatra saṃsthitaḥ (spa0 2 ni0 4  ślo0)   iti

plain_english: Others offer all sense-actions and breath-actions into the self-restraint yoga-fire illuminated by knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: sarvāṇīndriyakarmāṇi prāṇakarmāṇi cāpare | ātmasaṃyamayogāgnau juhvati jñānadīpite

plain_english: Substance, austerity, yoga, self-study, and knowledge sacrifices are named; ascetics offer mental and breath activities into the one-pointed fire illuminated by knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: dravyayajñāstapoyajñā yogayajñāstathā'pare | svādhyāyajñānayajñāśca yatayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ | te ca sarvān-indriyavyāpārānmānasān  mukhanāsikānirgamanamūtrādyadhonayanādīnvāyavīyāṃśca  ātmano-manasaḥ saṃyamahetau yoganāmnyaikāgryavahnau samyak  jñānaparidīpite pūrayitavye niveśayanti-gṛhyamāṇaṃ viṣayaṃ  saṃkalpyamānaṃ vā tadekāgratayaiva parityaktānyavyāpāratayā  buddhā gṛhṇantīti tātparyam | yaduktaṃ śivopaniṣadi-   bhāve'tyakte niruddhā cinnaiva bhāvāntaraṃ vrajet | tadā  tanmayabhāvena vikasatyatibhāvanā | (vi0 bhai0 62 ślo0)   iti | evaṃ yogayajñā vyākhyātāḥ | evaṃ dravyayajñastapoyajño yogayajñaścoktalakṣaṇāḥ | svādhyāyajñānayajñāśca ye- te saṃprati lakṣyante-

plain_english: Some offer prana into apana and apana into prana; restraining both movements, they are devoted to breath-control.
sanskrit_cite: apāne juhvati prāṇaṃ prāṇe'pānaṃ tathā'pare | prāṇāpānagatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāmaparāyaṇāḥ

plain_english: Others with regulated food offer breaths into breaths; all sacrifice-knowers have sins destroyed, and prana rises as sound ending in om, distinguishing self-study and knowledge sacrifices.
sanskrit_cite: apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇān prāṇeṣu juhvati | sarve'pyete  yajñavido yajñakṣapitakalmaṣāḥ | prāṇam-udayamānaṃ nādaṃ praṇavādimātrālayāntam apāne-astaṃ  yāti svānandāntaḥpraveśātmani juhvatīti piṇḍasthairyātmā  svādhyāyaḥ | śiṣyātmanā ca nayānayagrahaṇāya kecit astaṃ  yāntamudīyamāne saṃveśya tadekīkāreṇāpavargadānāt ātmani  śiṣyātmani ca śodhanabodhanapraveśanayojanarūpe svādhyāyayajñe  svaparānandamaye pratiṣṭhitamanasaḥ | ata eva pūrakaḥ  prathamamuktaḥ caramaṃ recakaḥ | prathamena ca pādena  viṣayabhogāntarmukhīkaraṇam | dvitīyena  mahāvidehadhāraṇākramādviṣayagrahaṇāya niḥsaraṇaṃ dhvanyate | ataśca svādhyāyayajñebhyo'nye jñānayajñāḥ | ete  evoktavyāpārapariśīlanāvaśaparipūritasvātmaśiṣyātmamanorathā  ḥ dve'pyete gatī nirudhyāhāraṃ viṣayabhogātmakaṃ niyamya  prāṇān-sakalacittavṛttyudayān prāṇeṣu-paranirānandollāseṣu  juhvati-kumbhakapraśāntyārpayanti | sarve caite  dravyayajñātprabhṛti jñānayajñāntaṃ yajñasya tattvajñāḥ  tenaiva ca  kṣapitakalmaṣāḥ-samūlonmūlitabhedavāsanāmayamahāmohāḥ

plain_english: Those who eat the nectar left from sacrifice go to eternal brahman; without sacrifice there is no world, and sacrifice nourishes the faculties while leaving self-rest.
sanskrit_cite: yajñaśiṣṭāmṛtabhujo yānti brahma sanātanam | nāyaṃ  loko'styayajñasya kuto'nyaḥ kurusattama | yajñena śiṣṭam-āhṛtaṃ yajñācca-nijakaraṇatarpaṇarūpāt  avaśiṣṭaṃ-svātmaviśrāntirūpaṃ  parānandanirānandātmakamamṛtaṃ bhuñjānā api yathecchaṃ  saṃsṛjyante brahmatayeti  taduparamyate'tirahasyasphuṭaprakaṭanavācālatāyāḥ | atra ca  bahutaro rahasyaraso'ntaḥ saṃlīnīkṛto'pi  niviḍatarabhaktisevāsaṃprasāditagurucaraṇaprāptasaṃpradāyamahau.  sadha-samīkṛtadhātūnāṃ carvaṇādiviṣayatāṃ  bhūtārthāsvādahetutāṃ ca pratipadyate | atra ca vyākhyāntarāṇi  ṭīkākāraiḥ pradarśitāni | tānyasmadgurupādaniruktāni ca  svayameva sacetasaḥ saṃpradhāryantām iti kimanyena hanta  vyākhyātṛvacanadūṣaṇāvinodanena | tadupakrāntamevopakramyate

plain_english: Many sacrifices spread from brahman's mouth; knowing them as means, one is freed from bondage.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ bahuvidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe | karmajānviddhi  tānsarvānevaṃ jñātvā vimokṣyase | sarve caite yajñāḥ brahmaṇo mukhe-dvāre upāyatve kathitāḥ | teṣu karmaṇāmanugamo'sti | evaṃ jñātvā tvamapi bandhanāt  mokṣameṣyasi

plain_english: Knowledge-sacrifice is better than material sacrifice, because all action is completed in knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: śreyāndravyamayādyajñājjñānayajñaḥ parantapa | sarvaṃ  karmākhilaṃ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate | atra tvayaṃ viśeṣaḥ-dravyayajñātkevalājjhānadīpito yajñaḥ  śreṣṭhaḥ | kevalatā ca mayaṭā sūcitā | yataḥ sarvaṃ karma  jñāne niṣṭhāmeti

plain_english: Know that through prostration, questioning, and service, reality-seers teach knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: tadviddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā | upadekṣyanti te  jñānaṃ jñāninastattvadarśinaḥ | tacca-jñānaṃ praṇipātena-bhaktayā  paripraśnena-ūhāpohatarkavitarkā-dibhiḥ sevayā-abhyāsena jānīhi | yata evaṃbhūtasya tava jñānino-nijā eva  saṃvittiviśeṣānugṛhītā indriyaviśeṣāḥ tattvam upa-samīpe  dekṣyanti-prāpayiṣyanti | tathāhi te tattvameva darśayantīti  tattvadarśinaḥ | uktaṃ hi   yoga eva yogasyopāyaḥ | ṛtambharā tatra prajñā | (yo0 sū0 1, 48)   iti | anye jñāninaḥ puruṣāḥ-iti vyākhyāyamāne  bhagavānsvayamupadiṣṭavāṃstadasatyam-ityuktaṃ syāt | evamabhidhāne ca prayojanamanye'pi lokāḥ praṇipātādinā  jñānibhyo jñānaṃ gṛhṇīyurna yathākathañciditi  samayapratipādanam

plain_english: Knowing this, you will not again fall into delusion; you will see all beings in yourself and in me.
sanskrit_cite: yajjñātvā na punarmohamevaṃ yāsyasi pāṇḍava | yena  bhūtānyaśeṣeṇa drakṣyasyātmanyatho mayi | ātmani mayi-matsvarūpatāṃ prāpte ātmani-iti sāmānādhikaraṇyam | athośabdaḥ pādapūraṇe | ātmana īśvarasya sāmye ko'pi  viśeṣa uktaḥ | asāmye vikalpānupapattiḥ | sarvaṃ karmākhilam-iti yaduktaṃ tatsphuṭayituṃ  prathamaślokenādharmo'pi naśyati-iti vadan sarvaṃ karma-iti  dvitīyena saṃskāraleśo'pi nāvatiṣṭhate-iti sūcayan akhilam-iti  vyācaṣṭe api cet-ityādi saṃśayātmanaḥ-ityantam-

plain_english: Even if you are the greatest sinner among all sinners, you will cross all sin by the raft of knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: api cedasi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ | sarvaṃ  jñānaplavenaiva vṛjinaṃ santariṣyasi

plain_english: As a blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, Arjuna, the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes.
sanskrit_cite: yathaidhāṃsi samiddho'gnirbhasmasāt kurute'rjuna | jñānāgniḥ  sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasātkurute tathā

plain_english: Nothing here is as pure as knowledge; the yogin perfected by yoga finds it in the self in time.
sanskrit_cite: nahi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitramiha vidyate | tatsvayaṃ  yogasaṃsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati

plain_english: The faithful, intent on that, with restrained senses, obtains knowledge; having obtained knowledge, one quickly attains supreme peace.
sanskrit_cite: śraddhāvāṃllabhate jñānaṃ tatparaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ | jñānaṃ  labdhvā parāṃ śāntimacireṇādhigacchati

plain_english: The ignorant, faithless, doubting self perishes; there is no world, other world, or happiness for the doubting self. Knowledge-fire arises through practice-born certainty, and nothing equals knowledge in purity.
sanskrit_cite: ajñaścāśraddadhānaśca saṃśayātmā vinaśyati | nāyaṃ  loko'sti na paro na sukhaṃ saṃśayātmanaḥ | samiddho'bhyāsajātapratipattidārḍhyabandhena jñānāgrirbhavati  yathā tathā prayatanīyamiti | pavitraṃ hi jñānasamaṃ nāsti | anyasya saṃvṛdhdyā pavitratvaṃ na vastuta ityatiprasaṅgabhayānna  pratāyate | pavitratāṃ cāsya svayaṃ jñāsyati suprabuddhatāyām | atra ca śraddhāgamastatparavyāpāratvaṃ jhagityeva  āstikatvādasaṃśayatve sati utpadyate | tasmādasaṃśayavatā  gurvāgamādṛte na bhāvyaṃ-saṃśayasya sarvanāśakatvāt | sasaṃśayo hi na kiṃcijjānāti-aśraddadhānatvāt | tasmāt  niḥsaṃśayena bhāvyamiti vākyārthaḥ | sakalādhyāyavisphārito'rthaḥ ślokadvayena saṃkṣipyate-

plain_english: Actions do not bind the self-possessed one who has renounced actions by yoga and cut doubt by knowledge; renunciation of actions comes through yoga alone.
sanskrit_cite: yogasaṃnyastakarmāṇaṃ jñānasañchinnasaṃśayam | ātmavantaṃ na  karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya | yogenaiva karmaṇāṃ saṃnyāsa upapadyate nānyathā iti vicāritaṃ  vicārayiṣyate ca

plain_english: Therefore, having cut with the sword of knowledge the doubt born of ignorance and seated in the heart, stand in yoga and arise, O Bhārata.
sanskrit_cite: yata evam   tasmādajñānasambhūtaṃ hṛtsthaṃ jñānāsinātmanaḥ | chitvaivaṃ  saṃśayaṃ yogamātiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhārata | saṃśayaṃ chitvā yogaṃ-karmakauśalamātiṣṭha uktakrameṇa | tataśca uttiṣṭha-tvaṃ svavyāpāraṃ kartavyatāmātreṇa kuru iti  śivam

plain_english: Here the summary verse declares that action preceded by mere desire alone satisfies the good-possessing sense-powers divinities.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   vidhatte karma yatkiñcidakṣecchāmātrapūrvakam | tenaiva  śubhabhājaḥ syustṛptāḥ karaṇadevatāḥ | iti  śrīmahāmāheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe caturtho'dhyāyaḥ
